issue.title: updates: common-state pts gap strands buffered updates (sequence-box state advance)
issue.body:
### Version

`github.com/gotd/td v0.160.0` (standard `updates.Manager` wiring: dispatcher handler, persistent SQLite state storage, persistent access hasher).

### What did you do?

In a **private chat** (common state), a bot streamed a long reply by editing one message repeatedly. The client's final text froze at an earlier snapshot (or ended empty) while other Telegram clients showed the full message.

Debug logs show the common-state (`logger:"updates.pts"`) sequence box losing buffered updates.

### What did you expect to see?

Every edit applied in order; the final text matching the server. A difference's state advance must not strand updates that were delivered live.

### What did you see instead?

Only a subset of the edits reached the handler. From one capture in a private chat:

- Wire: 30 `UpdateEditMessage`, sequential pts `145491 → 145526`.
- Manager: 5 × `Gap detected`, 19 × `Out of gap range, postponed`, 4 × `Outdated update, skipping`, 2 × partial `Pending updates applied` (one `accepted_count:7`).
- Result: only 17 of 30 edits dispatched; one message stored 3156 chars ending on the streaming cursor, another stored empty.
- `update_state.pts` still reached `145526` — the counter caught up while the edit dispatches were dropped.

### Mechanism (as I read it)

`internalState.getDifference` (`state.go`):

1. clears the gap buffers (`s.pts.gaps.Clear()`, etc.) but does not reconcile the sequence box's `pending`;
2. replays `diff.OtherUpdates` through `sequenceBox.Handle`;
3. calls `setState(diff.State)`, advancing the box state.

If the difference's `OtherUpdates` do not fill contiguously from the current state, `sequenceBox.Handle` re-buffers them (`gapRefetch`). The subsequent `setState(diff.State)` jumps the state past them, and `applyPending` then drops them as `gapIgnore` — the `Outdated update, skipping` lines above.

### Minimal reproduction sketch

Seed state `Pts=N`; deliver a live pts update at `N+2` (gap at `N+1`) so it buffers; return an `UpdatesDifference` with `State.Pts=N+2` and no `OtherUpdates`; then deliver a contiguous update to trigger `applyPending` — the `N+2` update is dropped.

### Not #1852

#1852 is the channel `channelDifference.timeout` cooldown in `state_channel.go`. This is the **common-state** path (`state.go` / `sequence_box.go`), used by private chats and basic groups, which has no such timeout; the proposed fix there does not cover this. Possibly the same family as the closed #1623.

### Notes

- Reported from [tele](https://github.com/sorokin-vladimir/tele), tracked there as [sorokin-vladimir/tele#267](https://github.com/sorokin-vladimir/tele/issues/267).
- tele works around the class by intercepting some update types (`UpdateReadHistoryOutbox`, `UpdateEditMessage`/`UpdateEditChannelMessage`) at the raw `UpdateHandler` level before pts-tracking, but the underlying common-state loss remains.

comments.body:
We hit the same drop with another update type: `UpdateReadHistoryOutbox`.

A read receipt arrives on the wire while a gap is open, so the sequence box buffers it. Then the difference moves the state past it, and `applyPending` skips it as outdated. On screen the messages we sent stay unread, and nothing fixes that until the next read receipt.

In tele we work around it by taking the two outbox-read updates off the raw envelope before the manager sees them (`internal/tg/outbox_hook.go`).

I have a question about #1854, because we would like to delete that workaround when the fix is released. The PR dispatches the updates that a difference replays, which covers the case in this issue. Does it also cover a buffered update that the difference does not replay at all?

Our regression test for the workaround does exactly that: state is `Pts=100`, a read receipt arrives live at `Pts=106` (so the gap is 101-105), and `getDifference` answers with `State.Pts=130` and no `OtherUpdates`. The receipt is dropped.

If a difference is meant to be the full truth for its whole range, then dropping it is correct, and the workaround stays on our side. I just cannot tell which of the two it is from the code.
